source_text: Educunt eum extra castra. Blasphemia expellitur. Ecclesia non communicat tenebris.
orientation: Origen is interpreting the punishment of the blasphemer from Leviticus 24, applying it spiritually to the church's separation from darkness.
pass_a_gloss: They lead him out beyond the camp. Blasphemy is expelled. The church does not share with darkness.

choices.why: Preserves the spatial sense of expulsion from the community, matching the Leviticus punishment and the spiritual separation Origen draws.
Keeps the passive force of the Latin, emphasizing that blasphemy is driven out rather than leaving on its own.
Renders the fellowship sense of communico, which carries the ecclesial meaning of communion and participation.
Keeps the moral-spiritual sense of darkness as the realm opposed to the church, echoing the light-darkness contrast in early Christian moral teaching.

pass_b_english: They lead him beyond the camp. Blasphemy is expelled. The church shares nothing with darkness.

last_rejected.why: Latin is passive but implies 'he' (the blasphemer) is expelled; English makes abstract 'blasphemy' the subject, changing agency and sense.
last_rejected.ruling: 'Blasphemia expellitur' is impersonal/passive: 'blasphemy is expelled.' No agent 'he' is specified; English correctly renders the Latin.
